paper_metadata.title: Synthetic data generation with hybrid quantum-classical models for the financial sector

summary: The paper studies a 5-qubit hybrid quantum-classical GAN (HQGAN) for synthetic financial data generation on Banco BV FGTS approval data, using a quantum circuit generator with angle embedding (Ry rotations) and controlled-Z entanglement plus a classical neural-network discriminator. It compares this against a classical GAN baseline (805,600 generator parameters, 183,969 discriminator parameters) over 5,449 epochs and finds the classical GAN consistently better: HQGAN diverges around mid-training and shows higher, erratic MSE, while the classical model’s MSE decreases and stabilizes.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical GAN (HQGAN) for synthetic financial data generation, using a quantum circuit as generator and a classical neural network discriminator; compared against a classical GAN baseline on Banco BV FGTS approval data.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid quantum-classical generative adversarial network with quantum generator and classical discriminator
algorithm.ansatz: Angle embedding with Ry rotations plus parameterized ansatz layers with controlled-Z entanglement
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 5449 epochs; additional truncated run at approximately 2500 iterations to inspect divergence

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each feature is encoded via an angle embedding circuit using Ry rotations; dataset padded with two additional zero-valued features to fit 2^NG output constraint with NG=4 data qubits
problem_formulation.objective_function: Adversarial training objective of GANs: min_G max_D E_x[log D(x)] + E_z[log(1 - D(G(z)))] with BCE loss used in implementation
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Partial measurement and ancilla qubit used to induce nonlinearity; dataset padding to 16 features; no explicit penalty formulation

problem_instance.description: Synthetic generation of approved-client financial records for Banco BV FGTS withdrawal approval case study

dataset_specification.description: April 2022 to July 2022; 16 features originally, 2 discarded (target and time); one categorical feature ordinal-encoded; features normalized to [0,1] with min-max scaling; two extra zero features padded for quantum generator compatibility

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discard target and time features; ordinal encode the single categorical feature; min-max normalize all features to [0,1]; pad with two zero-valued features to reach 16 features
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare HQGAN and classical GAN using loss convergence and MSE distance between synthetic and original data; additional experiment truncating training at ~2500 iterations

implementation_details.classical_solver: PyTorch neural network discriminator; classical GAN baseline implemented in PyTorch
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Ordinal encoding and min-max scaling; feature padding for quantum model

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: HQGAN loss initially stable then diverges around halfway through training; classical GAN shows more typical convergence behavior

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not claim or demonstrate any asymptotic or empirical speedup for the HQGAN; it reports comparative performance only.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No demonstrated quantum resource advantage; 5-qubit simulator-based HQGAN with 30 generator parameters and 2145 discriminator parameters.
limiting_factors: Classical GAN outperformed HQGAN on MSE and showed more stable convergence.
HQGAN loss diverged midway through training and remained erratic in MSE.
No asymptotic complexity analysis or speedup claim is provided.
Simulation-only study on a 5-qubit circuit does not establish practical quantum advantage.

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states simulations were executed on the quantum simulator Kuatomu; no real QPU was used.
num_qubits reported from NG=4 data qubits plus NA=1 ancilla qubit.
circuit_depth reported from Fig. 3 caption stating depth k=1.
speedup_order set to none_proven because the paper does not characterize asymptotic quantum speedup.
The paper explicitly states that the classical GAN performed better on the reported MSE metric and that HQGAN failed to learn the financial data patterns adequately.

experiments.description: Fully classical GAN baseline used for comparison against the HQGAN on the Banco BV FGTS dataset.
key_results: Classical GAN showed more typical convergence behavior than HQGAN.
Classical GAN MSE decreased consistently and stabilized toward the end of training.
After truncating training to ~2500 iterations, classical GAN still improved in MSE while HQGAN remained erratic.
